definition: a conjugate: one of a pair of things joined or related in a fixed way (conjugate of a complex number; conjugate acid)
to give the inflected forms of a verb in order; to join together in a pair (conjugate a verb; conjugate with another cell)
embodied in human or bodily form (the devil incarnate; evil incarnate)
to embody or give bodily form to a spirit, idea or quality (to incarnate a god; she incarnates the ideal)
a thing that is inserted or fitted in, such as a leaflet in a magazine or a part set into a larger one (a newspaper insert; a drill insert)
to put, fit or place something into something else (insert a coin; insert a paragraph)
being in a place, or existing now (present at the meeting; the present king; the present situation)
the current time, or a gift (at the present; a birthday present)
to give formally, introduce, show or offer for consideration (present an award; present a paper; the case presents problems)
a repeat showing of a broadcast or film, or a repeat of an event (reruns of old sitcoms; a rerun of the race)
to run again, or to show again (rerun the test; rerun the episode)
a reconsideration or fresh look (a radical rethink of the plan)
to think about again, often changing one's mind (rethink the strategy; rethink the whole question)
